definitions.explanation: A general term for anything worn on the feet, including shoes, sandals, slippers, and traditional Japanese footwear such as geta and zori.

examples.japanese: {履物|はきもの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{脱|ぬ}いで→脱ぐ：00518_nugu⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
⟦{玄関|げんかん}→玄関：05003_genkan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{履物|はきもの}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧⟦{並|なら}んでいる→並ぶ：00605_narabu⟧。
examples.english: A lot of footwear is lined up in the entryway.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{旅館|りょかん}→旅館：01049_ryokan⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{館内用|かんないよう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{履物|はきもの}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{用意|ようい}→用意：01746_youi⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: This ryokan provides indoor footwear for guests.

notes:
A broad category word covering all types of footwear. More common in formal signs, traditional settings, and written instructions than in casual speech, where ⟦{靴|くつ}→靴：00725_kutsu⟧ (shoes) is the default.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {履物|はきもの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{脱|ぬ}ぐ→脱ぐ：00518_nugu⟧ (to take off footwear)
- {履物|はきもの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{揃|そろ}える→揃える：01952_soroeru⟧ (to line up footwear neatly)
- {履物|はきもの}⟦{禁止|きんし}→禁止：02643_kinshi⟧ (no footwear allowed)

USAGE:
Often seen on signs at temples, schools, and traditional buildings where shoes must be removed. While ⟦{靴|くつ}→靴：00725_kutsu⟧ refers specifically to Western-style shoes, {履物|はきもの} encompasses everything from ⟦{下駄|げた}→下駄：03984_geta⟧ and ⟦{草履|ぞうり}→草履：04048_zouri⟧ to modern sneakers.
